articleTitle: Implementing an Intelligent Steam and Electrical Load-Shedding System for a Large Paper Mill: Design and Validation Using Dynamic Simulations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: An intelligent load-shedding system (ILSS) was designed and implemented in a paper mill to ensure power system stability after the steam turbine generator transitions from back-pressure operating mode to isochronous mode upon loss of the electric grid. The innovative approach taken to validate and optimize the operation of the system in a closed-loop environment by using dynamic simulation is presented. Modeling of the double-extraction steam turbine representing real-time processes was performed. The purposes for implementation of the ILSS were to maintain safe operating conditions and increase the reliability of the mill while minimizing operating costs and capital losses during unplanned events.

articleTitle: Application of Undervoltage Protection to Critical Motors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: Undervoltage protection is commonly used to protect motors from damage during abnormal conditions and to prevent breaker-fed motors from re-accelerating after a restoration of bus voltage. This protection method has the unfortunate consequence of introducing the possibility of a nuisance trip when VT's fail. This paper explores fundamentals of under voltage protection as well as pros and cons of different methods that can be deployed to prevent VT failure from causing costly outages. Case studies will be presented as well as methods which include both monitoring of hardwired VT status contacts and internal relay algorithms.

articleTitle: Unique Challenges for Resistance Grounding of High Harmonic Content Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: Neutral-grounding resistors (NGR) for industrial power systems are often selected without consideration of the nature of the loads on the system. Where a significant proportion of system demand is from adjustable-speed drives (ASD), unexpected performance problems, such as the NGR continually running hot without a detected ground fault, or NGR failure, can result. A significant factor is the use of ASD's that are not galvanically isolated from the power system-typical of six-pulse drive applications.

articleTitle: Process Control Networking - Bridging Between Process Control and Information Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: Many Pulp, Paper and Forest Industry sites use programmable logic controllers, distributed control systems or coordinated adjustable speed drive systems installed on a network. Most of the control systems interface with operators through computers run via commercially available off the shelf operating systems, hardware and network switches. These process control systems are also required to be connected to the business network which is often connected through firewalls to the internet. The internet connection is necessary to keep applications software, operating system software and antivirus software up to date. Because of this connectivity the information technology and the process control departments in a company must work together to develop a standard process control network. This paper summarizes the process used to develop a standard of one such company.

articleTitle: Most Common Mechanisms and Reasons for Electric Motor Failures in Industry
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: Electric motors used in the petrochemical industry are specified and designed for a minimum of 25 years of service life and at least 5 years of uninterrupted operation for [1] induction machines and synchronous [2] machines. Original equipment manufacturer engineers are designing to meet these requirements using modern design software, the latest materials, improved manufacturing processes and better mechanical configurations and cooling techniques, the reality is that many of these motors will fail prematurely in the first years of operation. This paper discusses the most common contributing factors of medium and high voltage induction and synchronous motor failures in the petrochemical industry. These contributing factors include; design flaws, manufacturing defects, incorrect selection of motor enclosures, maintenance issues and motor protection. This paper will help end users understand the importance of the mechanisms that lead to critical motor failure and maintenance practices designed to help keep equipment in optimum condition. This paper does not discuss specific original equipment manufacturing issues; but instead focusses on general mechanisms related to early motor failures based on root cause analysis, experience history and end-user feedback.

Author Keywords: Electric motor mechanical and electrical failures

articleTitle: Strategies for Reliable Arc Flash Detection in Low-Voltage Switchgear
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: Reliably detecting the ignition of an arc flash inside low-voltage metal enclosed switchgear using an arc flash detection system presents a number of technical challenges and requires careful system design to provide maximum equipment and personnel protection. The proper placement of sensors throughout the switchgear is critical to ensuring reliable arc flash detection. Given the large number of potential switchgear design variations, the best way to ensure reliable arc flash detection is through verification of sensor placement by creating true arcing events at a high power test lab using worst-case switchgear configurations in which the detection system will be applied. This paper will briefly discuss the tradeoffs between fiber optic and wired point sensors and will provide extensive treatment of methods to determine sensor placement, sensitivity and quantity within a given low-voltage switchgear design as well as strategies to avoid nuisance operation of the arc flash detection system.

articleTitle: Vintage Low-Voltage Motor Control Centers - Replace or Upgrade?
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: Low-voltage motor control centers are universally applied in process industries. These electrical assemblies are perhaps one of the most dynamic in industry, ever changing as low-voltage motor loads are constantly added and modified in response to necessary process revisions and upgrades. As existing low-voltage motor control centers (MCCs) approach 40 to 50 years age, industry users are challenged with a decision to replace vintage MCCs approaching their end of life, or consider upgrade of existing assemblies. This paper will discuss upgrade versus replace alternatives, addressing UL 845 North American industry standard requirements and how this affects design, installation and maintenance of both upgraded and new MCCs. Application issues including considering the cost of replacing load cables versus reuse of existing cables, high-resistant pulsing ground systems and opportunities for process improvements and network communications that leverage the latest technology will be discussed. Finally, a case study comparing the alternative of replacing an existing MCC versus a field upgrade based on changing out all exiting starter and feeder circuit breaker units and an estimate of the total installed cost for both MCC replacement and upgrade for this application will be reviewed.

articleTitle: The Problem of Ground Faults on Overhead Lines with High Earth Return Resistance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to consider the impact of high resistivity soil on ground current from fallen overhead lines via a hypothetical earth path resistance calculation. A second major thrust is consideration of solutions to the related problem of how to detect and automatically de-energize overhead lines when they fall. The relevance of specific types of automatic ground fault protection for downed overhead lines is considered based upon current magnitudes that flow with high earth resistance in the return path. Failing to consider proper soil preparation, including moisture, and suitable grounding can produce dangerous conditions by generating high earth path resistances. This can produce relays unresponsive to ground faults. Long cables as replacements for overhead lines are also considered.

articleTitle: In Memoriam [Professor Robert D. Lorenz (31 March 1946 - 27 January 2019]
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: A brief biography of Professor Robert D. Lorenz is given highlighting his professional achievements. He was a strong supporter of the IEEE Pulp and Paper Industry Committee (PPIC) since becoming a member in 2000, and was a member of the PPIC Drives and Controls Subcommittee. He co-authored many papers that were presented at the IEEE Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conferences (PPFIC). He co-authored and co-presented two papers at the 2018 IEEE PPFIC conference in Appleton, WI.

articleTitle: Panel discussion: Managing and maintaining obsolete drive systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE IAS Pulp, Paper and Forest Industries Conference (PPFIC)
abstract: Summary form only given. A complete record of the panel discussion was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings. During the late 1980's and early 1990's, many sectors of the Forest Products Industry were increasing production, which led to new equipment and major upgrades and speed increases of existing equipment, all of which required new drive systems. Many of those systems are now at, or past, end of life, but are still in operation. This panel discussion will cover a number of topics around how to manage and maintain obsolete drive systems to minimize business (and sleep) risk.
